name: oracle-ai-data-platform-workbench-informatica-migrator
description: Migrate Informatica ETL onto Oracle AI Data Platform from Codex: mappings become PySpark notebooks, workflows become AIDP jobs carrying the session dependency graph, Quartz schedules and a declarable timezone, with worklets expanded. Reads IDMC/IICS cloud mapping JSON and PowerCenter 10.x repository XML; 8.x and 9.x are refused by a version gate rather than mis-migrated. The transformation compiler is deterministic and needs no model -- an OpenAI key only widens what the rules cannot reach, behind a validator and a hallucination check. Reads and writes are catalog-addressed, so no JDBC URLs or credentials appear in a generated notebook. Anything that cannot be converted faithfully becomes an explicit review item with a named reason and a rebuild path, never a silent approximation.

interface.shortDescription: Self-contained Informatica to Oracle AIDP migrations from Codex.
interface.longDescription: Migrate Informatica ETL onto Oracle AI Data Platform from Codex: mappings become PySpark notebooks, workflows become AIDP job definitions. The plugin bundles its Python engine and stages it to ~/.aidp-infa-migrator/engine on SessionStart, so no separate clone is required. Reads IDMC/IICS cloud mapping JSON and PowerCenter 10.x repository XML; 8.x and 9.x are refused by a version gate rather than mis-migrated. The compiler is deterministic and needs no model: 36 transformation types convert, 14 more are reported with a named reason and a rebuild path, and 72 Informatica expression functions are supported. An OpenAI key only widens what the rules cannot reach. Workflows carry the session dependency graph, Quartz schedules and a declarable timezone, with worklets expanded; tasks that have no AIDP equivalent are reported with their configured values rather than dropped. Reads and writes are catalog-addressed, so no JDBC URLs or credentials appear in a generated notebook. A construct the tool cannot convert faithfully becomes an explicit review item, never a silent approximation.
defaultPrompt: Use infa-migrator-overview to pick the right skill for analyzing an Informatica export, migrating mappings to notebooks, reconciling a migrated target, or deploying to AIDP.

Use infa-migrator-bootstrap on first-time setup to confirm ~/.aidp-infa-migrator/engine, Python deps, and -- only if deploying -- ~/.oci/config and an ACTIVE AIDP cluster. No API key is needed for the migration itself.
Use infa-migrate-mapping for the main run: point it at an export directory and it writes notebooks, job definitions, target DDL and a review report.
